interactive_elements — vanilla-JS interaction build notes + the universal engine + building the curated set.
instance_embeds — per-provider (YouTube/Vimeo/Spotify) markup + the file:// facade caveat.
maps_leaflet / timelines / paper_review_browser / task_demo / scrollytelling — build mechanics extending their canonical recipes.
cinematic_background — the full-bleed scroll background build + chart_card_DEFAULT_in_cinematic_mode.
inspector_panel — the verbatim Verify panel build + the two JSON islands.
before_after_slider / card_deck_swipe / stat_callouts / assets / audio_music / visual_transitions / references_section — recipe pointers + implementation extensions.
honest_accuracy_scorecard (E2) — predictions-vs-real + model-vs-baseline tables; mark the better value per metric even when the baseline wins; data inlined, never recomputed.

numbers_read_not_hardcoded — every displayed number reads from data/model at runtime; never hardcoded, never recomputed in-page.
_note: Programmer-side IMPLEMENTATION detail per visual component — the load-bearing JS/CSS, file:// caveats, measurement fixes, and the components that only the Programmer builds (charts mechanics, cinematic background, inspector panel, science-paper widgets, audio engines). Single self-contained HTML file, no build step, no framework. Allowed CDNs: Vega-Embed, Leaflet.js (plus PDF.js, D3.js where noted).
_canonical_recipe_library: The single source of truth for component RECIPES (structure + visual intent + when-to-use) is ../../frontend-design/references/components.json. This file does NOT restate those recipes — for a component that components.json already defines (hero, stat callout, card deck, entity cards, chart/map frame, audio player, signature media card, scrollytelling, before/after, guess-reveal, data table, figure, references footer) build from components.json and use the entry here ONLY for the extra implementation detail that extends it. Where an entry below duplicated a recipe, it now carries a `_recipe` pointer to the components.json key plus only the programmer-specific extension. Color scales -> ../../frontend-design/references/design_tokens.json data_color_scales. Motion timing -> ../../frontend-design/references/motion.json. Interaction engine + Pudding recipes -> ../../frontend-design/references/interaction_playbook.json. Chart-craft (intent->type, annotation, axis polish, encoding) -> ../../dataviz-craft/references/.

charts_vega_lite._recipe: Chart framing/caption/source-note/theme-styling recipe = components.json chart_frame (the canonical recipe). Chart-TYPE selection (intent->type), annotation layers, axis/label de-clutter and encoding craft = ../../dataviz-craft/references/ (chart_chooser / vega_recipes / annotation_layers / axis_label_polish / encoding_craft). This entry extends both with the load-bearing Vega-Embed MECHANICS (mount/measurement/centering/scale.zero/labelExpr) that only live here.
rules: Inline data only (from analyst.json data_tables — no external fetches).
Style from designer.json — if unspecified: no gridlines, muted palette, "width": "container".

DARK-STAGE GUIDE TEXT (the cinematic background is ALWAYS on + embedChart sets spec.background='transparent', so every chart sits over the dark stage): build the chart's Vega `config` from the dark `_config_block` in ../../dataviz-craft/references/axis_label_polish.json — it sets config.title.color AND config.title.subtitleColor (a SEPARATE property; setting only color leaves the subtitle at Vega's DARK default = invisible), config.axis.labelColor/titleColor, config.legend.labelColor/titleColor all LIGHT, plus light-on-dark gridColor/domainColor. NEVER ship a chart relying on Vega's default guide-text colors over the dark stage (the subtitle/axis/legend text goes dark-on-dark — PIT-62). The opaque .chart-card surface (cinematic_background.chart_card_DEFAULT_in_cinematic_mode) gives the chart a dark backing but does NOT set the text color — that is the config's job.
Highlight the key data point as specified in content.highlight.
Use column names from the data_table for encodings.

Center the rendered chart output: keep the mount block-level (display:block; width:100%) and center the rendered SVG with `.vega-embed svg{display:block;margin:0 auto}`, so a chart Vega renders narrower than the container (facet / repeat / concat / step-sized charts ignore width:container) is centered, not left-aligned. NEVER set `.vega-embed` to display:inline-block — a shrink-to-fit wrapper makes Vega measure 0 width and width:container charts render invisible (0×H).

CINEMATIC PHOTO/STILL BACKGROUND: the cinematic stage runs on EVERY blog, so when cinematographer.json meta.mode is `photographic` or `generative` ('cinematic' is the backward-compat alias for 'photographic'), a chart can sit over a full-bleed photo/AI-still background — wrap it in an opaque .chart-card surface by default so it stays legible (see cinematic_background.chart_card_DEFAULT_in_cinematic_mode). In `data_driven` mode the dimmed signature chart is itself the background spine; an in-column detailed copy still takes the card. This is the surface the chart sits on and is orthogonal to the width/measurement fix in responsive_embed below — keep both.
pitfalls: Give the actual vegaEmbed() target a dedicated block-level mount element (width: 100%; min-width: 0; display: block). Do not embed into an anonymous shrink-to-fit child div.
For composite charts (facet, repeat, vconcat, hconcat, small multiples), specify child widths and spacing explicitly. columns belongs at the facet spec top level, not inside the facet object.

Composite/faceted/step-sized charts IGNORE width:container and render at their own (often narrow) width, so they LEFT-ALIGN inside a block mount. Center the rendered SVG with `.vega-embed svg{display:block;margin:0 auto}` so these are centered, not stuck to the left. Never use `.vega-embed{display:inline-block}` for this — an inline-block wrapper measures 0 width and breaks every width:container chart (they render invisible).

When a quantitative domain is clipped, negative-only, log-scaled, or otherwise should not include zero, do not trust the default baseline. Bars/areas usually need explicit x2/y2; year axes and bounded metrics usually need scale.zero = false plus an explicit domain.
labelExpr and other Vega expressions use Vega expression syntax, not full JavaScript. Prefer helpers like format(...); do not call JS methods such as .toFixed() inside Vega expressions.

A MARK property takes only LITERAL values — never a {condition:...}/encoding object on `mark` (e.g. `"align":{condition:...}` / `"dx":{condition:...}` / `"color":{condition:...}`). It is INVALID Vega-Lite and fails SILENTLY: text/point labels lose their x/y binding and clump at the axis. For per-datum styling, split the data into FILTERED LAYERS (one literal-mark layer per condition) or move the conditional onto a real ENCODING channel where `.condition` IS valid (encoding.color.condition, etc.). validate.py Section 19 flags a `condition` inside a `mark` object (vega_conditional_on_mark, PIT-64).

POINT/SCATTER/DOT marks must not escape the plotting frame: a datum beyond an explicit scale.domain draws OUTSIDE the plot area (over the axis/card). Two-part fix — (1) give scale.domain HEADROOM past the data max/min, or OMIT domain so Vega auto-fits the extent; AND (2) set `"clip": true` on the point/scatter mark so nothing renders outside the frame even if a domain is tight. Bars/areas are bounded by the baseline; points are not, so they need clip + headroom (axis_label_polish.json point_overflow_rule, PIT-65). (This is the INNER-plot overflow — distinct from PIT-03's outer-SVG axis/legend overhead overflowing the card, fixed by svg_must_fit.)

responsive_embed._why: width:container is measured the instant the inline <script> runs (often during page parse, before layout). On a long/heavy page that measurement returns 0, so the SVG renders 0px wide and is INVISIBLE. The block-mount / never-inline-block rules above fix the CSS half but are NOT sufficient; this fixes the measurement half. Embed every simple width:container chart through this helper. The helper ALSO (a) wraps its WHOLE body — including the embed call — in try/catch so one chart throwing cannot blank its siblings (FM1 fault isolation), (b) re-paints when the mount later becomes visible (tab/accordion/cinematic-reveal/`data_driven` spine), not just on resize (FM3), and (c) degrades to the inlined data as a static <table> when the Vega CDN failed to load (FM5).
embed_js: // Canonical responsive chart embed — use for every width:container chart.
// Do NOT call vegaEmbed(el, spec) directly with width:container: measure the
// real pixel width after layout, fall back if still 0, and re-render on resize
// AND on first-visible. The ENTIRE body is wrapped so one chart's throw can never
// abort the shared <script> and blank every sibling + the hero (FM1).
function embedChart(id, spec, fallbackTable){
try {
// FM5: Vega CDN blocked / failed to load -> render the inlined data_table as a
// static <table> fallback instead of leaving a dead empty mount (extends the
// interaction-degradation doctrine to charts). fallbackTable is the optional
// inlined-data <table> HTML string (or a fn returning it) for this chart.
if (typeof vegaEmbed !== 'function') {
var fb = document.getElementById(id);
if (fb && fallbackTable) fb.innerHTML = (typeof fallbackTable === 'function') ? fallbackTable() : fallbackTable;
console.error('embedChart('+id+'): vegaEmbed unavailable (CDN blocked) — static table fallback');
return;
spec.background = 'transparent';
function cw(){
var el = document.getElementById(id); if(!el) return 0;
var w = Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().width || el.clientWidth || 0);
if(w < 40){ var p = el.parentElement; w = p ? Math.round(p.getBoundingClientRect().width) : 0; }
return Math.min(w < 40 ? 640 : w, COLUMN_MAX);  // COLUMN_MAX = page column max-width, e.g. 720
function paint(){ try { var el = document.getElementById(id); if(!el) return;
spec.width = cw(); vegaEmbed(el, spec, {actions:false, renderer:'svg'}).catch(function(e){ console.error('embedChart('+id+') embed:', e); }); }
catch(e){ console.error('embedChart('+id+') paint:', e); } }
function go(){ (window.requestAnimationFrame || window.setTimeout)(paint, 0); }
if(document.readyState === 'loading') window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', go); else go();
var t; window.addEventListener('resize', function(){ clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(paint, 200); });
// FM3: a chart that starts in a display:none / 0-box container (tab, accordion,
// cinematic-revealed beat, data_driven spine) measures 0 at first paint and stays
// blank when later shown. Re-paint on first-visible + on the mount's own box growing.
var el0 = document.getElementById(id);
if (el0 && typeof IntersectionObserver === 'function') {
var io = new IntersectionObserver(function(es){ es.forEach(function(en){
if(en.isIntersecting){ paint(); io.disconnect(); } }); }, {threshold:0.01});
io.observe(el0);
if (el0 && typeof ResizeObserver === 'function') {
var lastW = 0;
var ro = new ResizeObserver(function(){ var w = Math.round(el0.getBoundingClientRect().width);
if(Math.abs(w - lastW) > 8){ lastW = w; clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(paint, 120); } });
ro.observe(el0);
} catch(e){ console.error('embedChart('+id+'):', e); }
responsive_embed.fault_isolation_RULE: FM1 — each chart/interaction setup is its OWN IIFE wrapped in try{…}catch(e){console.error(...)}. All charts are emitted into ONE shared <script> that runs each setup sequentially; the FIRST synchronous uncaught exception aborts the whole block, blanking every later chart AND the hero (the exact bug the Auditor hand-fixed: a `draw(null,…)` deref blanked 3 charts + the hero). Calling embedChart (whose body is now wrapped) is not enough on its own — any per-chart prep you write BEFORE/AROUND the embedChart call (building `values`, deriving a scale, a `specFn(cw())` that derefs data) runs in the shared block too, so wrap each chart's WHOLE setup: `(function(){ try { var spec = buildSpecForChartN(); embedChart('des_NN', spec, tableNN); } catch(e){ console.error('chart des_NN setup', e); } })();`. One throw then logs and the next chart still mounts. validate.py Section 14 WARNs a single <script> with >=2 chart mounts and <1 try; render_capture.js correlates a throw to mass-blanking as `cascade_script_abort`.
responsive_embed.no_sentinel_baseline_RULE: FM2 — never pass a callee a sentinel it will deref. A chart/interaction's baseline / 'at-rest' render must be called with REAL data, never `draw(null,…)` / `render(null)` / `update(undefined)` as a 'draw nothing yet' placeholder — the callee derefs it and throws (which, per FM1, can abort the shared block). Every value-accessor treats `null`/`""`/`undefined`/`{}`-typed (an object where a number is expected) as MISSING and SKIPS that datum; never `Number({value,flag})` (→ NaN → `width:NaN%` paints nothing, PIT-05). Compute the at-rest state from the inlined data_table / client_model, exactly as the published baseline.
responsive_embed.composite_charts: Facet/repeat/concat/step-sized charts IGNORE width:container and render at their own width — set explicit child widths and center the SVG (see pitfalls). The helper above is for simple width:container charts.
responsive_embed.history: Recurred twice. _fix_chart_css.py (CSS inline-block->block) and auditor fix_6_chart_mount_width only fixed the CSS/mount half; bare width:container kept rendering invisible on heavier pages until this measure-after-layout helper became the default. The try/catch body-wrap + first-visible re-paint + CDN-load fallback were added after a single `draw(null)` throw in the shared <script> blanked 3 sibling charts and the hero on a real run (FM1/FM2/FM3/FM5).

fit_and_legibility._why: Distinct from responsive_embed above (which governs the chart's WIDTH/measurement so width:container charts aren't 0px). This governs FIT inside the container and LEGIBILITY over a background. A Vega SVG routinely renders WIDER than spec.width: axis titles, tick labels, and especially a side legend are drawn OUTSIDE the plotting area, so the final <svg> is spec.width + that overhead. With the chart in a fixed-width (frosted) break-out container, that extra width spills past the container's right edge onto the bare page/photo — the off-center / overflowing-chart symptom even after the width fix.
fit_and_legibility.svg_must_fit: ALWAYS clamp the rendered SVG to its container: `.chart-card svg{ max-width:100% !important; height:auto; display:block; margin-inline:auto; }` (apply to the actual visual-container/.chart-card wrapper, whatever its class). max-width:100% caps the SVG at the container width so axis/legend overhead can never overflow; height:auto preserves aspect ratio; margin-inline:auto centers any SVG that Vega rendered narrower than the container (composite/step-sized charts). The `!important` defeats Vega-Embed's inline sizing.
fit_and_legibility.legend_orient: Set `legend:{orient:'top'}` (or 'bottom') on charts with a legend. A default RIGHT-oriented legend adds width on the right and, on a wide or near-container chart, gets clipped at the right edge (and is the biggest single source of the 'renders wider than spec.width' overflow). A top/bottom legend stretches the chart vertically instead, which never clips horizontally. For one series, drop the legend entirely.
fit_and_legibility.frosted_surface_in_cinematic: Over a photo/AI-still cinematic background (mode `photographic` or `generative`; 'cinematic' is the backward-compat alias for 'photographic'), wrap EVERY chart/table in an opaque-or-frosted surface so it reads over the image (this is the same wrapper that fit must stay inside). Use the opaque `.chart-card` from cinematic_background.chart_card_DEFAULT_in_cinematic_mode for very busy backgrounds, or the softer frosted backing (semi-transparent dark + backdrop-filter:blur, no hard/gold border) described in ../../frontend-design/references/layout.json immersive_cinematic_layout.visuals_over_photos_frosted_backing. CRITICAL pairing: the backing must always be >= the chart, and the chart is kept inside it by the svg_must_fit rule above — so the SVG never spills outside the dark area onto the bare image. The break-out width + centering math for that surface is layout.json immersive_cinematic_layout.break_out_wider (use margin-inline:calc((100% - TARGET)/2); NEVER margin:auto on a wider-than-parent block, NEVER transform:translateX(-50%)).

interactive_elements: Vanilla JS only, inline in the HTML.
Implement the interaction spec from designer.json step by step: initial state → trigger → transition → payoff.
Include a visible affordance (button, drag handle, etc.).

Standardize on the universal engine: a `state` object + one `render()/update()` + (for scroll/step UIs) a `steps[]` array of functions. The portable Pudding-grade recipes (scrollytelling via position:sticky + IntersectionObserver, explorable_recompute, personal_input, data-bound guess_then_reveal, self_drawing_line, animated_transitions) are in ../../frontend-design/references/interaction_playbook.json — read it before building any non-trivial interaction.

For an EXPLORABLE centerpiece: inline the Analyst's client_model (from analyst.json / code/) and recompute the output live on control changes (debounce sliders); animate the chart update (D3 transition or re-embed). Guess/reveal values MUST be data-bound (computed from the data_table / client_model), never hardcoded pixel widths.

BUILDING THE SET (interaction.json with centerpiece + supporting[]): build the hero centerpiece AND every supporting[] playground the Editor curated. Each playground is an INDEPENDENT universal_engine instance (its own state + render() + steps[]) mounted in its bound section (supporting[].section) — do NOT share one state object across playgrounds. Tag each root data-int="int_NN" + data-ana (+ optional non-provenance data-play-out="int_NN" on its live readout); register a verify_map entry per int_ id and a run_cells Pyodide cell when it recomputes a number. Build only what the Editor curated; an unearned widget caps visual_design at 3.

RECIPES for the supporting archetypes are in ../../frontend-design/references/interaction_playbook.json -> recipes: scored_quiz (guess-then-reveal + reader-vs-precomputed-distribution), playable_game / interactive_demo_minigame (a tiny self-contained 'experience the finding' loop), tune_the_assumption (topic-agnostic explorable_recompute — slider sets an assumption delta, re-derive vs the cached published baseline), personal_input_where_you_land (reader enters a value -> pull their row from the inlined data_table / a client_model percentile -> 'you're here'). Each uses universal_engine, inlines the Analyst client_model/data_table (never raw files), tags data-int+data-ana, ships a <noscript>+reduced-motion fallback, and a matching Pyodide run_cell when it produces a number.

FAULT ISOLATION (FM1, MANDATORY): every playground's setup is its OWN IIFE wrapped in try{…}catch(e){console.error('int_NN setup', e)} — and so is every chart's setup (charts_vega_lite.fault_isolation_RULE). The page emits all of these into ONE shared inline <script> that runs sequentially; the FIRST synchronous uncaught throw aborts the entire block, so one playground that derefs a missing field would silently blank every later chart/playground AND the hero. Wrapping each setup means a throw logs to console and the next playground still mounts. Do NOT rely on the universal engine's internals to catch this — wrap at the mount site: `(function(){ try { /* state + render() + steps[] + wireControls() */ } catch(e){ console.error('int_NN setup', e); } })();`. (render_capture.js flags >=2 unrendered mounts + a console error as `cascade_script_abort`; validate.py Section 14 WARNs a multi-mount <script> with no try.)

NO SENTINEL BASELINE (FM2): the initial / 'at-rest' render() MUST run on REAL data — never call the renderer with a sentinel a callee will deref (`draw(null,…)`, `render(undefined)`, `update({})` as a 'nothing selected yet' placeholder); compute the baseline state from the inlined data_table / client_model exactly as the published figure. Every value-accessor treats null/""/undefined and a `{value,flag}`-typed object as MISSING and SKIPS it (never `Number({...})` → NaN → `width:NaN%` paints nothing, PIT-05). A guess/reveal bar width is data-bound, never a hardcoded px.

HANDLER try/catch + EDGE-VALUE SAFETY (FM5): wrap the BODY of every feature-side interaction handler (slider `input`/`change`, button `click`, select `change`, drag, keydown) in try/catch — `el.addEventListener('input', function(e){ if(vOn())return; try { recompute(); } catch(err){ console.error('int_NN input', err); } });` — so one bad reader gesture logs instead of throwing into the event loop and wedging the widget. Keep the `if (vOn()) return;` Verify-coexistence guard as the FIRST line (before the try). The recompute must be SAFE AT EDGE VALUES: driving a slider to its min / max / an empty input must not divide-by-zero, index past the array, or `Number()` an object — clamp/guard so the readout degrades to a sane value, never throws or prints NaN. (The Playtester drives an edge value and asserts no throw — playtest_drive.js FIRES step.) When a JSON island / client_model is parsed at setup, wrap the `JSON.parse(...)` in try/catch and fall back to the static at-rest number.

CDN/MODEL-ABSENT FALLBACK (FM5): if a chart inside a playground needs Vega and `typeof vegaEmbed!=='function'`, OR the playground depends on Pyodide/a lib that didn't load, the playground must still reveal its at-rest number from the static DOM (the <noscript>/JS-off degradation path the Playtester checks) — extend the existing interaction-degradation doctrine: never leave a dead empty control region when a CDN is blocked.

instance_embeds._note: When designer.json has an item with type 'instance', implement based on embed_type. Tag all instance embeds with data-des like any other visual element. Provider-agnostic: support YouTube, Vimeo, and Spotify — match the embed to the instance's provider/source_url; never hardcode a story to one platform. The presentation recipe (rounded frame, caption, facade-vs-live decision) = components.json audio_player.embed; this entry carries the per-provider markup + the file:// caveats.
instance_embeds.file_origin_caveat: CRITICAL: Data2Story pages open from file:// (no server). A live YouTube iframe player then has a null origin/referrer and fails with 'Video player configuration error' (Error 150/153, with a 'Watch on YouTube' overlay) — oEmbed returning 200 only means embedding is allowed, NOT that it plays on a null origin. So DEFAULT YouTube/Vimeo/video instances to a click-through thumbnail facade, not a live iframe.
instance_embeds.youtube: Default = thumbnail FACADE (robust on file:// and http): ▶Watch on YouTube — {label} + a caption. Style the facade 16:9 with a centered play overlay. Take {ID} from the instance's source_url/embed_url. Only use a live
instance_embeds.vimeo: Same FACADE-first treatment as YouTube (a live Vimeo iframe is more file://-tolerant than YouTube but still safest as a facade on file://): ▶Watch on Vimeo — {label} + a caption (Vimeo has no fixed img.* thumbnail URL like YouTube's hqdefault.jpg — take {thumbnail_url} from the instance's poster/thumbnail field, or the Vimeo oEmbed `thumbnail_url`). Reuse the SAME 16:9 .ytfacade styling. Take {ID} from the source_url/embed_url. Only when served over http(s) use a live .
instance_embeds.spotify: <iframe src="{embed_url}" width="100%" height="152" frameBorder="0" allow="autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; fullscreen; picture-in-picture" loading="lazy"></iframe>. Spotify embeds tolerate file:// better than YouTube; if one misbehaves, fall back to a facade linking to the track. Wrap in a styled container with rounded corners, subtle shadow, caption below.
instance_embeds.audio_url: <audio controls src="{url}"></audio> with label and caption.

pdf_preview: Load the paper PDF from assets/paper.pdf (copy from DATA_DIR if needed).
Render specific pages into <canvas> elements. Add page navigation (prev/next) and zoom controls.
For 'page region' specs: render the full page and use CSS to highlight/crop the specified region.
Container responsive, max-width 720px, subtle drop shadow. Add a 'View full paper' link to the original URL.
citation_network_d3: Use D3.js via CDN for force-directed graph layout. Inline the citation data from designer.json or analyst.json.
Nodes: circles sized by citation count, colored by type (this paper = accent, references = muted, citers = secondary).
Edges: lines with arrows showing citation direction.
Interaction: hover to see paper title + year, click to open link.
Force simulation: charge repulsion + link distance, with drag to reposition. Container full-width, 500px height, zoom/pan via d3-zoom.

review_visualizations.radar_chart: Inline SVG with <polygon> for each reviewer's scores. Axes = review dimensions. Overlay all reviewers with different colors + legend.
review_visualizations.concern_treemap: D3.js treemap layout. Each rectangle = a concern category, sized by count/severity. Color by category. Click to see reviewer quotes.
review_visualizations.disagreement_heatmap: HTML table with cells colored by score (green=high, red=low). Rows=reviewers, columns=dimensions.

maps_leaflet: _recipe: The canonical map recipes are components.json map_frame (standard boxed map: dark/muted CARTO tiles, data-scaled markers, legend, scroll-wheel-zoom trap fix) and components.json rich_map (the immersive full-bleed geographic CENTERPIECE: fitBounds, rich photo popups, highlighted marquee node, scroll_trap_fix). Build from those; the lines below are the Leaflet wiring detail that extends them.
Use Leaflet via CDN: <link> + <script> from unpkg.com/leaflet.
Tile layer: prefer dark/muted CARTO tiles (dark_all / positron) per map_frame, not raw OSM, so the map matches the theme; OSM is the free no-key fallback.
Inline GeoJSON or marker data directly in the HTML (from analyst.json data_tables). For choropleth: inline the geo boundaries + data join.
Markers should have popups with relevant info on click.
Map container responsive, ~400-500px height (a marquee centerpiece goes taller / full-bleed per rich_map).

FM4 — MANDATORY map-sizing fix (a Leaflet map in a hidden / 0-height container renders grey, half-painted, or mis-tiled until told its real size): (1) give the .leaflet mount a FIXED CSS height BEFORE L.map() initialises (e.g. `#mapMount{height:480px}` / the full-bleed height) — a 0-height container at init yields a broken map; (2) call `map.invalidateSize()` on FIRST-VISIBLE via an IntersectionObserver on the mount (a map inside a tab / accordion / cinematic-revealed beat / a column that lays out after init measures 0 at init and stays grey until invalidated); AND (3) call a DEBOUNCED `map.invalidateSize()` on window `resize`. Wrap the whole map setup in its own try/catch IIFE (FM1). Reference: `(function(){ try { var el = document.getElementById('mapMount'); var map = L.map(el, {scrollWheelZoom:false}); /* tiles + markers + fitBounds */ if (typeof IntersectionObserver==='function'){ var mio = new IntersectionObserver(function(es){ es.forEach(function(en){ if(en.isIntersecting){ map.invalidateSize(); mio.disconnect(); } }); }, {threshold:0.01}); mio.observe(el); } var mt; window.addEventListener('resize', function(){ clearTimeout(mt); mt=setTimeout(function(){ map.invalidateSize(); }, 200); }); } catch(e){ console.error('map mapMount setup', e); } })();` render_capture.js measures `.leaflet-container` boxes — a >0 mount with 0 tiles painted, or a 0-height container, is a hard finding.

FM5 — CDN-load guard: if Leaflet failed to load (`typeof L === 'undefined'`), do NOT call L.map() (it throws and, per FM1, can abort the shared <script>). Guard `if (typeof L !== 'function' && typeof L !== 'object'){ /* render the inlined location/data table as a static <table> fallback into the mount */ console.error('Leaflet unavailable (CDN blocked) — static table fallback'); return; }` at the top of the map IIFE, mirroring embedChart's vegaEmbed guard.

KEYBOARD-READOUT PARITY (a11y, MANDATORY when a marker/control drives a live readout; PIT-61): when a marker (or any map control) updates a live `[data-play-out]` readout on the MOUSE path (hover/click), the KEYBOARD path MUST update the SAME readout — never only `marker.openPopup()`. (1) Make each marker keyboard-reachable + labelled: give its element `tabindex=0`, `role="button"`, and a descriptive `aria-label` (e.g. `marker.getElement().setAttribute('tabindex','0')` after add, or build markers as `L.marker(latlng,{keyboard:true})` and set role/aria-label on `marker.getElement()`). (2) Wire BOTH a `focus` listener AND a `keydown(Enter/Space/ArrowRight)` listener that call the SAME readout-update fn the mouse `click`/`mouseover` calls — transfer the interactive_hero keydown pattern (wireHalf's `el.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){ if(e.key==='Enter'||e.key===' '||e.key==='ArrowRight'){ e.preventDefault(); updateReadout(d); } })` + `el.addEventListener('focus', function(){ updateReadout(d); })`), so focus-or-key produces the identical `[data-play-out]` change as a mouse hover/click. Reference: `function bindMarkerKbd(mk, d){ var el = mk.getElement(); if(!el) return; el.setAttribute('tabindex','0'); el.setAttribute('role','button'); el.setAttribute('aria-label', d.label); el.addEventListener('focus', function(){ updateReadout(d); }); el.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){ if(e.key==='Enter'||e.key===' '||e.key==='ArrowRight'){ e.preventDefault(); updateReadout(d); mk.openPopup(); } }); }` — call it for every marker (mk.getElement() exists after the marker is added to the map). (3) Size the zoom controls to the >=44px hit-area: `.leaflet-control a{width:44px;height:44px;line-height:44px}` so the +/- controls clear the keyboard/touch target. The Playtester's a11y/keyboard-readout-parity check (playtest_drive.js) emits report_types.json `interaction_keyboard_no_readout` if a keyboard gesture leaves `[data-play-out]` unchanged while the mouse path moves it.
timelines: Implement as a horizontal or vertical scrollable element. Each event is a node on the axis with date + label.
Click or hover to expand details. Vanilla JS + CSS, no library needed.

Avoid fixed-width absolute-positioned timelines inside the ~720px story column. If the sequence has many labels, switch to a responsive numbered-card timeline that stays readable on desktop and mobile.
paper_review_browser: Implement as collapsible accordion panels (one per paper).
Each panel header: tag badge (accepted/rejected), paper title, subtitle with scores, chevron toggle.
Toggle via onclick="this.classList.toggle('open')" + CSS max-height transition (0 → 2000px, 0.4s ease-out).
Panel body: score badges, audit verdict badge (color-coded by severity), key findings as <ul>, blockquote for auditor quotes, external link.
Badge colors: PASSED/accepted = teal, CRITICAL/HIGH = coral, LOW/PARTIAL = amber. Pure CSS animations + inline onclick handlers.
task_demo: Interactive tabbed panel showing a concrete input→process→output example from the paper.
Structure: header (title + subtitle) → tab bar → tab panels.
Tab switching: vanilla JS toggling .active class on buttons and panels.
Panels scroll independently: max-height: 500px; overflow-y: auto with styled scrollbar.
Content uses monospace font (.demo-code) with semantic color classes. Pure CSS + inline onclick handlers.
scrollytelling: _recipe: The scrollytelling recipe (sticky graphic + scrolling steps, IntersectionObserver active-step, the universal state+render+steps[] engine) is canonical in ../../frontend-design/references/interaction_playbook.json (recipes.scrollytelling + universal_engine); components.json scrollytelling is the one-line summary. The lines below are the build mechanics + the load-bearing MOT6 reveal-guard that only live here.
Use IntersectionObserver to detect which step is in view.
Each step triggers a visual change (map zoom, chart filter, highlight).
Sticky visual panel + scrolling text column layout. Smooth CSS transitions between states.

SCROLL/LIST-REVEAL (progressive enhancement, MANDATORY): content is visible by default. Gate the `opacity:0` initial state behind a root class JS adds (`document.documentElement.classList.add('js-reveal')`), write the CSS as `html.js-reveal .reveal:not(.in) > *:not(figure):not([data-vis]):not(.chart){opacity:0; transform:translateY(8px); transition: opacity var(--dur-md) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-md) var(--ease-out); transition-delay: calc(var(--i,0) * var(--stagger));}` + `html.js-reveal .reveal.in > *{opacity:1; transform:none;}`, and mark every above-the-fold `.reveal` (and any under reduced motion) `.in` immediately instead of waiting on the observer. NEVER apply the opacity gate to charts/maps/visuals — they render async (Vega/Leaflet paint after the observer fires) and can stay blank; the `:not(figure):not([data-vis]):not(.chart)` exclusion handles this, so tag chart/map mounts with data-vis or .chart. A reveal that can hide content on load is a HARD FAIL (quality_rubric MOT6): visuals and above-the-fold content must be visible without IntersectionObserver. Copy the exact CSS+JS from ../../frontend-design/references/motion.json -> choreography.reveal_visible_by_default; do not paste the bare `.reveal > *{opacity:0}` form.

cinematic_background._note: Build the full-bleed scroll-driven CINEMATIC BACKGROUND on EVERY blog — it is a MANDATORY stage with NO off path. cinematographer.json meta.mode is one of `photographic` (primary), `generative` (fallback) or `data_driven` (fallback) — 'cinematic' is a backward-compat ALIAS for 'photographic'. Implement the scenes (cin_xx) per cinematographer/references/cinematic_recipes.json. All three modes share the SAME pinned layer + IntersectionObserver-toggles-.active engine. The plain editorial column is NOT an output of this component — build it ONLY in the impossible case that cinematographer.json is absent or has zero scenes (a pipeline error; cinematic is mandatory and always writes scenes). NEVER emit a cinematic on/off toggle or any `.cinematic-off`/`html.cinematic` class gate (or sessionStorage state) — the cinematic CSS is UNCONDITIONAL (do not scope it under `html.cinematic ...` or `html:not(.cinematic-off) ...`). The stage is always on; the only adaptation is `prefers-reduced-motion` (freezes motion, keeps the imagery), never an off switch.

mode_dispatch.photographic: The primary mode (the WC exemplar). Each scene's background is a verified Scout sct_ / Designer des_ REAL photo (or video) — INCLUDING rest scenes. Build the crossfade-photo background per `build` below + the fit_modes (cover/framed). A REST is a held/dimmed REAL photo (the adjacent sct_/des_ image rendered `framed` and/or under a heavier scrim), NEVER a `kind:gradient`/`kind:color` layer and NEVER two rests in a row — a real photo is always on screen, crossfading into the next, with no black scroll gap (PIT-54).
mode_dispatch.generative: Fallback when relevant real imagery can't be sourced. Each scene is either a `kind:color|gradient` layer (a CSS gradient from designer.json's theme — NO , NO media_ref) OR a `kind:image` whose media_ref is a REGISTERED des_ AI atmosphere/metaphor still (object-fit:cover, gentle ken-burns) stacked over the gradient. Show the visible credit 'AI-generated atmosphere — illustration' on each AI still. Same crossfade engine; interleave gradient 'rest' layers (LEGITIMATE here only — there are no real photos to hold; this does NOT license a gradient rest in photographic mode). See cinematic_recipes.json generative_atmosphere.
mode_dispatch.data_driven: Fallback for a data-heavy topic with no fitting imagery: PIN the story's signature annotated chart as the scroll spine (see data_driven_chart_spine below) over a `kind:gradient` backdrop. Same IntersectionObserver — but instead of crossfading photos it reveals the chart's annotations/series as each beat crosses the middle. See cinematic_recipes.json data_driven_spine.

chart_card_DEFAULT_in_cinematic_mode._why: When a cinematic stage runs (always, but acutely in photographic/generative mode), charts/stat blocks sit OVER full-bleed photo or AI-still backgrounds. A bare chart (transparent background, dark axis text) is illegible over a bright or busy image — the Auditor flags it and a card has to be patched in afterward. Make the card the DOCUMENTED DEFAULT so legibility holds over ANY background on ANY topic, not a per-blog afterthought.
chart_card_DEFAULT_in_cinematic_mode.rule: When cinematographer.json meta.mode is `photographic` or `generative` (a photo/still background), EVERY chart / data-viz / map / stat callout that can sit over that background renders on an OPAQUE surface card by default (the .chart-card recipe below). The card gives the foreground its own readable surface independent of whatever image is behind it. This is orthogonal to — and does NOT replace — the responsive_embed width fix above (that fix governs the chart's width/measurement; this governs the surface it sits on). Keep both. (In `data_driven` mode the dimmed signature chart IS the background spine; an in-column detailed copy of that chart still takes the card.)
recipe_css: /* Opaque foreground surface for any visual sitting over a cinematic background. */

.chart-card{ background: var(--surface); padding: clamp(16px, 3vw, 28px); border-radius: 10px; /* design_tokens radius.card 6-10px */ border: 1px solid var(--line); box-shadow: 0 8px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.28); }
/* --surface is opaque by token definition (a step from --bg); never use an rgba()/translucent fill here — the photo must NOT bleed through and reduce contrast. */
chart_card_DEFAULT_in_cinematic_mode.apply: Wrap each in-scene visual's mount in . The card is the surface; the existing visual-container margins/centering and the responsive_embed helper still apply inside it. Stat callouts, Vega charts, Leaflet maps and interactive blocks over a background all take the card.
chart_card_DEFAULT_in_cinematic_mode.backward_compatible: Emit .chart-card over photo/still backgrounds (mode photographic/generative, or the legacy alias 'cinematic'). Do NOT card visuals in the ONLY case there is no cinematic stage at all — the impossible no-scenes pipeline-error fallback where charts stay in a clean centered column.

build: One pinned full-bleed layer behind the text (position:sticky; top:0; height:100vh — or position:fixed with the text column at higher z-index). The story's text scrolls OVER it. This same pinned stage is used by all three modes.

CHART/STAT LEGIBILITY (photo/still-background default): every chart, data-viz, map and stat callout that sits over a photo or AI-still background renders on an OPAQUE .chart-card surface (see chart_card_DEFAULT_in_cinematic_mode above) so it reads over any background. This is in addition to the responsive_embed width fix, not a replacement for it.
PHOTOGRAPHIC / GENERATIVE scenes — for each scene cin_xx (in order): a background (or a muted

Crossfade by toggling an `.active` class (active scene opacity 1, others 0) via CSS `transition:opacity ~1.1s ease` — NOT a JS opacity tween and NEVER a forced-reflow restart (`void el.offsetWidth` is the #1 jank source). Switch the active scene with an IntersectionObserver on the text beats (rootMargin '-45% 0px -45% 0px'). Put `decoding='async'` on every background and call `img.decode()` on load to pre-decode (kills crossfade stutter).

FIT each photo background (cinematic_recipes.json fit_modes): `cover` for wide/atmospheric shots (full-bleed crop fine); `framed` for an object/portrait whose WHOLE subject must show — a blurred darkened cover copy as the backdrop + the real image object-fit:contain on top (full-bleed AND whole subject visible).

Apply GENTLE motion via CSS transition on `.active` (ken-burns idle scale 1.0 -> active ~1.03-1.05; ~1.03 for framed) — transform/opacity ONLY (compositor); never animate layout props, never an aggressive zoom.

TAGGING: tag each photo/still scene element data-cin='cin_xx' AND data-sct/data-des (from the scene's media_ref) so the scene and its verified source are both traceable. A `kind:color|gradient` scene is tagged data-cin only (no media_ref). A data_driven chart-spine layer is tagged data-cin + data-ana. No raw/unverified background PHOTO — ever; an AI atmosphere still must be a registered des_ and carry the 'AI-generated atmosphere — illustration' credit.
SCRIM: every text-over-background scene gets a readability scrim (gradient/wash per the scene's scrim spec). Legibility wins over the image / chart spine.

REDUCED MOTION + JS OFF: photographic/generative -> drop parallax/zoom/crossfade to static per-section scrimmed backgrounds (gradient layers need no JS, so a no-JS page still shows a coloured backdrop, never a blank column). data_driven -> show the signature chart with ALL annotations/series at once (no scroll-gated reveal). The page must read fully in every mode.
PERFORMANCE: lazy-load; decode only current+next; mobile srcset / video poster; keep total page weight low (a viral demo dies on a 30MB page).

data_driven_chart_spine._why: The data_driven fallback: a computational topic with no real imagery still ships a mandatory scroll background — the story's SIGNATURE annotated chart, pinned as the spine, its annotations revealing on scroll. Reuses the SAME pinned-layer + IntersectionObserver engine; only the active background is a chart, not a photo.
build: ONE pinned `.cin-bg`-style layer holds the signature chart (a Vega-Embed mount via the responsive_embed helper, or an inline SVG/D3) over a `kind:gradient` theme backdrop layer (NO media_ref). Dim/desaturate the chart (lower contrast, muted palette) and keep a scrim between it and the prose so the foreground copy wins.
The chart's data is INLINED from analyst.json data_tables (never refetched) — it is the analyst's signature finding, the same discipline as numbers_read_not_hardcoded.

As each text beat crosses the viewport middle, the SAME IntersectionObserver toggles `.active` on that beat, which reveals the matching chart annotation/series/highlight: an `.in` class on annotation layers (CSS opacity/transform transition) and/or a small state step that filters/highlights the chart (the scrollytelling sticky-graphic pattern applied to the BACKGROUND layer). The chart stays PINNED; only its annotations animate in.
TAGGING: tag the chart-spine layer data-cin='cin_xx' AND data-ana (the finding's ana_xx) so Verify traces the spine to its computation. The annotation reveals carry no separate id.

REDUCED MOTION + JS OFF: render the chart with ALL annotations/series shown at once over the gradient — fully readable, no scroll gating. The data spine degrades to a single complete annotated chart, never a blank backdrop.

A FULL detailed/interactive copy of the same chart can still appear as a normal in-column figure (in a .chart-card) where a beat calls for the reader to inspect it; the spine is the dimmed background version.

cinematic_background.reference: COPY THE TECHNIQUE FROM cinematographer/references/example_cinematic_scroll.html — it now carries BOTH the photographic demo (pinned-crossfade of verified photos) AND a clearly-delimited ABSTRACT-PATH demo (the data_driven chart-spine + generative_atmosphere gradient, reusing the same IntersectionObserver engine, plus a reduced-motion block that shows the full annotated chart at once). Details in cinematographer/references/cinematic_recipes.json (engine + recipes: pinned_crossfade [+ smoothness_CRITICAL] / fit_modes / ken_burns / parallax_depth / video_background / generative_atmosphere / data_driven_spine; readability_scrims; guardrails) + ../../frontend-design/references/interaction_playbook.json (the scroll engine).

inspector_panel._note: Build the in-page Inspector panel — the reader-facing front-end of the verify layer, a click-any-claim drawer embedded IN index.html (the reproducible notebook is the paper's from-raw-data coding verifier). MANDATORY on every blog (build: always), like cinematic_background and the BGM: every blog ships the Verify panel — there is no off mode. The panel is the in-page successor to the old standalone viewer.html (which is now only a redirect). You COPY the verbatim UI build; the Inspector fills the two JSON islands. Do NOT reimplement the panel from scratch.

copy_verbatim._why: The .v-* CSS, the toggle, the drawer/backdrop/toast markup, and the window.__verify IIFE are the load-bearing, topic-agnostic blocks. They are owned by the reference build and pre-tested on file://; retyping them invites the no-reflow / focus-trap / es5-leak / kind-renderer bugs the reference already solved.
copy_verbatim.rule: COPY ../../inspector/references/inspector_panel_reference.html VERBATIM into index.html — the three flagged blocks: (1) the `.v-*` <style> ('VERIFY INTERACTION LAYER — copy verbatim'); (2) the `#verifyToggle` button + the drawer/backdrop/toast markup ('VERIFY MARKUP — copy verbatim'); (3) the final `window.__verify` IIFE <script> ('VERIFY LAYER IIFE — copy verbatim'). Do not edit these blocks; the only per-blog edits are the two JSON islands and the publish wiring below.
copy_verbatim.drawer_no_reflow: The drawer OVERLAYS the page (fixed-position panel above the content); it does NOT push the body. Do not reintroduce the old viewer's `body{margin-right:440px}` reflow — it mis-sized full-bleed (100vw) sections and made the page jump on open.

json_islands_byte_identical._why: The on-disk verify/*.json are the auditable source of truth and the publish artifacts (also the inputs the downloaded notebook reproduces from); the inline islands are what the panel actually reads at runtime. If they drift, the audited provenance no longer matches what readers see.
json_islands_byte_identical.rule: index.html carries two inline islands the Inspector fills: `<script type="application/json" id="verifyMap">` (BYTE-IDENTICAL to verify/verify_map.json) and `<script type="application/json" id="runCells">` (BYTE-IDENTICAL to verify/run_cells.json). The Programmer leaves these islands in place (copied verbatim); the Inspector's generate_viewer.py writes the per-blog bytes. Do not hand-edit the island contents.
json_islands_byte_identical.escaping: When the islands are filled, any literal </script> is escaped as <\/script> and the JSON is serialised with ensure_ascii so raw multibyte chars / newlines do not break the JS parser.

inspector_panel.kinds: verifyMap[id].kind selects the drawer renderer: computation (claim + code slice + data_preview + expected_output + a Run panel) / media (real asset preview + source_url + license + identity, gallery for multi-asset) / generated (AI-asset preview + tool/model/prompt/disclosure + the real_default fallback) / fact (claim + categorised sources[] with per-source facts[]) / credits (a fact-shaped license/source aggregator rendered with a Credits badge). A runnable computation gets a Run button that re-executes the snippet in-browser (lazy Pyodide) and grades stdout against expected_stdout — letting the reader recompute the figure from its inlined data (the reproducible notebook does the full from-raw-data re-run).

publish_wiring._why: The panel's 'Download notebook' link points at the reproducible notebook (NB_PATH); the reader downloads it and runs it LOCALLY alongside the bundled verify/data/ inputs. There is NO Colab branch — the notebook is download-and-run-locally only.
publish_wiring.NB_PATH: Relative path to the reproducible notebook the panel's Download-notebook link points at (verify/<project>.ipynb). The only publish constant the Programmer leaves in the shell IIFE.
publish_wiring.open_cell_source: The 'Open the notebook cell ↗' button opens a fresh blank tab with the inlined run_cells[id].code in a <pre> — a RAW-CODE page (works on file://), NOT a Colab/notebook link.
publish_wiring.viewer_redirect: The panel lives IN index.html — that single file IS the verifiable artifact. New runs ship ONLY index.html; no separate viewer.html is emitted, and the Programmer does not build a standalone viewer. (Historically the Inspector emitted a viewer.html redirect for paper-link continuity; that was retired — previously-deployed blogs keep their own viewer.html on disk, unaffected.)

data_attr_tagging._why: The panel only makes an element clickable if it carries a data-* id that exists in verifyMap; this is the same traceability contract the Programmer already follows when tagging the page.
data_attr_tagging.rule: Tag every verifiable element with one of data-{ana,det,des,sct,cin} (reuse the existing five — do NOT introduce a new data-* attribute), value = the atomic id (e.g. data-ana="ana_01"). Decorative wrappers (<section>, <main>, .cin-stage and other structural shells) carry no id and are skipped; the INNERMOST tagged element wins on a click. Every data-* id on the page MUST exist as a key in verify_map.json (a dangling id is an auditor failure). This is the same tagging recorded in traceability.json — cross-ref ../../inspector/references/verify_map.schema.json (#/patternProperties id namespaces) and the Stage-5 data-* contract.
data_attr_tagging.cross_ref: Keep the page's data-* ids in lockstep with verify_map.json / traceability.json — the same ids drive both the provenance map and the panel drawer.

inspector_panel.reference: COPY THE BUILD FROM ../../inspector/references/inspector_panel_reference.html (the verbatim, self-contained panel UI — the .v-* CSS + #verifyToggle + drawer/backdrop/toast markup + the window.__verify IIFE, plus the two JSON islands it reads). Behaviour, the no-reflow overlay drawer, the kinds→renderers, the byte-identical-island rule, the lazy-Pyodide grading, and the publish wiring are documented in ../../inspector/references/inspector_panel_internals.json. The Inspector (inspector/SKILL.md) owns filling the islands and emitting verify/.

before_after_slider: _recipe: components.json before_after (two layered images/maps + a draggable divider via clip-path/overflow, works on touch+mouse, labeled states). Implementation note: vanilla JS drag handler on the divider sets the clip/overflow width; no library. Tag the figure data-des.
card_deck_swipe: _recipe: A card deck's CANONICAL layout is a VERTICAL grid — components.json card_deck (light browse) / entity_cards (scored profiles); do NOT default to a horizontal scroll-x carousel (interaction_playbook.json no_horizontal_scroll). The ONLY sanctioned horizontal paging is a SMALL discrete set (3-7) via interaction_playbook.json scroll_snap_stepper (native CSS scroll-snap + keyboard arrows + a dot rail). Implementation note: scroll-snap-type:x mandatory on the track, scroll-snap-align:center on fixed-width children; add the stepper's keyboard + IntersectionObserver dot-rail wiring. Tag data-des.

honest_accuracy_scorecard._note: Two honest credibility tables for a forecast/model story: (C1) a predictions-VS-real ✓/✗ table (what the model said for each item vs what actually happened), and (C2) a model-VS-naive-baseline metrics table (Brier / log-loss / accuracy on a held-out sample). The HONESTY is the point: show where the model was WRONG, and mark the BETTER value per metric EVEN WHEN THE NAIVE BASELINE WINS. This is the trust close — never a victory lap.
honest_accuracy_scorecard.data_is_inlined_never_recomputed: All numbers come INLINED from a precomputed JSON (e.g. an accuracy_28.json with the per-item predictions + the model/naive metric blocks) dropped into a `<script type="application/json" id="accuracyData">` island. The renderer READS that island and prints rows — it NEVER recomputes a metric in-page (no in-browser Brier/log-loss math). The Analyst computed them; the page only displays them. (Same discipline as every other number on the page — see numbers_read_not_hardcoded.)

C1_predictions_vs_real.build: A table (or per-group collapsible panels) with one row per item: the model's prediction (favourite + e.g. likely score / probability) and the REAL result, plus a ✓/✗ hit marker computed by COMPARING the two inlined fields (predicted_winner === actual_winner). Show losses honestly — do not hide or grey-out the ✗ rows.
C1_predictions_vs_real.hit_marker: var hit = (row.pred_winner === row.actual_winner); cell = hit ? '✓' : '✗'; // ✓ / ✗ — derived from the data, not authored per-row
C1_predictions_vs_real.upcoming_rows: If some items are not yet resolved (future fixtures), render the prediction with a neutral 'upcoming' state (no ✓/✗) from a separate inlined upcoming/fixtures list — never fabricate a result.

C2_model_vs_naive_mark_better_even_when_._why: The load-bearing honesty rule. A scorecard that only bolds the model's wins is propaganda. Mark the BETTER value PER METRIC within each test block — and when the NAIVE baseline is better on a metric, mark the NAIVE cell. The reader sees exactly where the model earns its keep and where it merely ties or loses.
C2_model_vs_naive_mark_better_even_when_.build: One block per test (e.g. 'these 28 played games' and an '8,000-match skill check'), two rows each (Model, Naive base-rate), columns = the metrics (accuracy, Brier, log-loss). For each metric decide the winner by its DIRECTION: accuracy is higher-better; Brier and log-loss are LOWER-better. Bold/accent only the winning cell.
C2_model_vs_naive_mark_better_even_when_.winner_logic: function better(modelVal, naiveVal, lowerBetter){ var mWins = lowerBetter ? (modelVal < naiveVal) : (modelVal > naiveVal); return { modelWins: mWins, naiveWins: (!mWins && modelVal !== naiveVal) }; }  // applied per metric: acc -> lowerBetter=false; brier,log_loss -> lowerBetter=true. A tie marks NEITHER. mk(win, txt) wraps the winner in <b style="color:var(--accent)">.
C2_model_vs_naive_mark_better_even_when_.honesty_in_prose: Pair the table with one honest sentence from editor.md (verbatim) that states the result plainly even when it's a tie/loss on the small sample (e.g. 'on the 28 games played the model and the naive baseline are a dead heat'). Tag the metrics block + that sentence with the SAME data-ana so Verify shows the scorecard's evidence.
C2_model_vs_naive_mark_better_even_when_.caption: A one-line caption stating metric directions: 'Lower Brier and log-loss are better; higher accuracy is better.'

honest_accuracy_scorecard.tagging_and_verify: Tag the scorecard region data-des + data-ana (the accuracy finding's ana_xx); register a verify_map entry (kind:computation) whose run_cell recomputes the metrics from the inlined data EXACTLY (deterministic — same figures as the table). The renderer binds by id (e.g. #scorecardTable / #scoreCardBody) and runs at end-of-body so the markup can live anywhere in the section.
honest_accuracy_scorecard.cinematic_mode: Over a cinematic photo background, wrap both tables in the opaque .chart-card surface (cinematic_background.chart_card_DEFAULT_in_cinematic_mode) so they stay legible.
honest_accuracy_scorecard.when: Any story resting on a model/forecast with (a) discrete predictions you can score against real outcomes and/or (b) a baseline you can beat (or honestly tie) on standard metrics. The single most credibility-building component for a forecast blog.

interactive_hero._note: A clickable HERO that is interactive when Verify is OFF and a single Verify provenance hit-target when Verify is ON (e.g. a 'pick a side' hero: each half runs the inlined client_model and reveals the picked side's outcome). This is the BUILD wiring of the verify-coexistence recipe — interaction-design side: ../../frontend-design/references/interaction_playbook.json verify_coexistence + the interaction role's references/interaction_recipes.json interactive_hero_verify_coexist.
the_three_build_rules: 1. The interactive sub-targets are `role="link" tabindex="0"` elements (NOT <button>/<a href>/<input>/<select> — i.e. NOT in the Verify engine's INNER_INTERACTIVE allow-list), laid over a CONTAINER that carries the provenance data-* (e.g. <div class="teaser" data-des="des_hero">). So under Verify a click on a half BUBBLES to the container's provenance hit.

2. EVERY feature handler starts with `if (vOn()) return;` where `const vOn = () => document.documentElement.classList.contains('verify-on');` — click, keydown(Enter/Space), and any hover/focus side-effect. Under Verify the gesture does nothing in feature-land and falls through to the Verify layer.
3. Feature code NEVER calls stopPropagation() (nor a preventDefault that swallows the bubble). The click must reach the container so the Verify delegated handler opens the drawer.
markup: <div class="teaser" data-edt="teaser" data-des="des_hero_video">  <!-- container carries the provenance data-* (ONE hit for the whole hero) -->
<!-- decorative overlays (chips/particles/bolt) use pointer-events:none + NO data-* so they never intercept the halves or the Verify hit -->
wiring_js: function pick(side){ if (vOn()) return; const p = MODEL.simulate(N)[side]; reveal(side, p); }  // recompute via the INLINED client_model — NEVER stopPropagation here
el.addEventListener('click', function(){ if (vOn()) return; pick(side); });            // Verify owns the click -> it bubbles to the container
el.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){ if (vOn()) return; if(e.key==='Enter'||e.key===' '){ e.preventDefault(); pick(side); } });
el.addEventListener('mouseenter', function(){ if (vOn()) return; setHover(side); });     // even hover side-effects guard
interactive_hero.recompute_is_the_real_model: The reveal RECOMPUTES via the SAME inlined Analyst client_model that produced the published headline (e.g. simulate(N) -> {side: p_champion}) — the at-rest published number and the reader's click are two readouts of ONE model. numbers_read_not_hardcoded._note: Reinforced cross-cutting rule for EVERY component above and below — already stated in SKILL.md Rules; restated here because it is the most-violated one.
numbers_read_not_hardcoded.rule: Every displayed number READS from analyst.json data_tables / the inlined client_model / a precomputed inlined JSON island AT RUNTIME — never typed as a literal into the HTML and never recomputed by you. Charts inline data_table values; stat callouts read content.value; the honest_accuracy_scorecard reads its inlined accuracyData island; an explorable/interactive_hero recomputes via the inlined client_model. THE ONLY in-page computation allowed is an explorable/interactive recompute running the Analyst's OWN client_model in response to reader input (the model running, not you guessing) — and it must reproduce the published figure at the baseline. If a number isn't in analyst.json / the model / an inlined precomputed island, it does not go on the page.
numbers_read_not_hardcoded.anti_pattern: Typing '26.3%' as a literal in the HTML, hardcoding a reveal/guess bar width in px, or recomputing a metric (Brier/log-loss) in-browser instead of reading the Analyst's precomputed value.

Wire the spin to playback via the `.playing` class on the .soundtrack wrapper (the disc spins IFF audio is playing): add `.playing` on play, remove it on pause. Embed the WC first-click autostart JS (sndKick) so the track starts on the reader's FIRST gesture anywhere (the closest to autoplay browsers allow — bare autoplay-with-sound on load is blocked). This is the components.json signature_media_card.autostart + scroll_to_start affordances implemented together: listen on 7 window events {passive:true} — scroll, wheel, touchmove, touchstart, pointerdown, keydown, click — each calling audio.play(), so the track can also begin AS THE READER SCROLLS (scroll_to_start) and not only on an explicit tap; a guard flag (sndKicked) prevents double-fire. A pure scroll/wheel does NOT grant audio activation, so LOCK IN only on the resolved play() promise: in .then() set sndKicked=true, set currentTime=0 so it plays from the start, ADD the `.playing` class (start the spin), reflect the button state (innerHTML to the pause glyph, aria-pressed="true"), then removeEventListener for all 7 events; in .catch() do nothing and keep listening for the next real gesture. The explicit play/pause button always remains (scroll-to-start is an additional affordance, never the only one). Wire the play/pause button to toggle audio.play()/pause(), toggle the `.playing` class in lockstep, and mirror the same button state — so the disc spins iff the audio is playing. Reference JS:

var sWrap=document.querySelector('.soundtrack'),sBtn=document.getElementById('sndBtn'),sAud=document.getElementById('sndAudio'),sLbl=document.getElementById('sndLbl'); function sndSpin(on){ if(sWrap)sWrap.classList.toggle('playing',!!on); } if(sBtn&&sAud){ sBtn.addEventListener('click',function(){ if(sAud.paused){sAud.play().then(function(){sBtn.innerHTML='❙❙';sBtn.setAttribute('aria-pressed','true');if(sLbl)sLbl.textContent='Sound on — playing';sndSpin(true);}).catch(function(){});} else {sAud.pause();sBtn.innerHTML='▶';sBtn.setAttribute('aria-pressed','false');if(sLbl)sLbl.textContent='Sound off — tap to resume';sndSpin(false);} }); sAud.addEventListener('pause',function(){sndSpin(false);}); sAud.addEventListener('play',function(){sndSpin(true);}); var sndKicked=false; var SND_EVENTS=['scroll','wheel','touchmove','touchstart','pointerdown','keydown','click']; function sndKick(){ if(sndKicked)return; try{sAud.currentTime=0;}catch(e){} var pr; try{pr=sAud.play();}catch(e){return;} if(pr&&pr.then){ pr.then(function(){ sndKicked=true; sBtn.innerHTML='❙❙'; sBtn.setAttribute('aria-pressed','true'); if(sLbl)sLbl.textContent='Sound on — playing'; sndSpin(true); SND_EVENTS.forEach(function(ev){window.removeEventListener(ev,sndKick);}); }).catch(function(){}); } } SND_EVENTS.forEach(function(ev){window.addEventListener(ev,sndKick,{passive:true});}); }

Song-vs-ambient knobs: a real SONG plays from the start (currentTime=0) at a MODERATE audio.volume (set e.g. sAud.volume=0.5..0.7 so it never blasts) — it may loop (add the `loop` attribute on <audio> for a short looping bed) OR play once (omit `loop` for a full song that should play through and stop). An ambient/instrumental BGM bed (incl. the classical-recording floor) typically loops; a vocal anthem typically plays once. The disc keeps spinning while it plays and stops on the 'ended'/'pause' event for a play-once track. Document the choice; either way it stays reader-controllable (the play/pause button always works) and respects a muted preference.

Render the track's attribution as a credit line beside the card and in the References footer: a clean sct_ uses scout.json sct_.license.attribution_text (a classical-recording floor credits the RECORDING's license/performer, not just the composer); a copyrighted demo track names the title / artist / source_url.

PUBLISH-GATE note (copyrighted self-hosted BGM): a best-fit copyrighted track self-hosted for the DEMO is a Designer des_ audio asset with publish_blocker:true and license 'All Rights Reserved — demo-only' + a source_url (NOT a clean sct_ — it must never masquerade as a license-allowlisted sct_ item to validate.py). The Auditor raises the ADVISORY copyrighted_audio_publish_blocker (flags, never blocks the demo build). When designer.json's BGM audio item is publish_blocker:true (or its asset license is demo-only/All-Rights-Reserved), the Programmer MUST render a footer / credits note: 'Soundtrack is a demo-only self-hosted track — license or swap it for a license-clean cue before publishing.' Prefer a license-clean track when one fits (publishable > gated); the license-clean classical RECORDING floor is always available as a clean fallback.
data_sonification_web_audio: Create an AudioContext on user interaction (click-to-play button — never autoplay audio with sound).
Map data values to oscillator frequency, gain, or playback rate per the designer spec. Use OscillatorNode for tones, GainNode for volume envelopes.
Provide a visible play/pause or step-through control. Sync visual animation with playback: highlight chart bars, timeline points, map markers, or cards as notes play.
Include a small legend explaining the mapping. Do not implement sonification as a detached tone card; attach it to the data visual it explains.
ambient_cues: Use Web Audio API OscillatorNode for short synthetic tones (avoid loading external audio files).
Trigger on the specified event (scroll into view, hover, click). Keep sounds subtle: 100-500ms, low volume.
Include a mute toggle, remember state in sessionStorage. Put the mute toggle near the affected interaction, not in a central audio block.
general_rules: NEVER autoplay audio with sound on page load — browsers block it and it annoys readers.
Always provide a visual play/pause control.
All audio must degrade gracefully: if Web Audio API is unavailable, the visual experience must still work fully.
Mobile: audio requires a user gesture to start — ensure the play button is touch-friendly (min 44x44px).
